title.value: Multi-Head Adapter Routing for Cross-Task Generalization
title.justification: The paper presents a novel technique, Multi-Head Adapter Routing (MHR), for achieving cross-task generalization in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
title.quote: In this paper, we investigate the role that adapter routing plays in its success and design new variants based on our findings... Hence, we propose MHR (Multi-Head Routing), which combines subsets of adapter parameters and outperforms Poly under a comparable parameter budget...

extractions.description: The paper introduces Multi-Head Adapter Routing (MHR), a technique in parameter-efficient fine-tuning to improve cross-task generalization by utilizing multiple heads in routing, allowing more fine-grained mixing of task parameters while maintaining efficiency.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on developing a method for fine-tuning machine learning models efficiently across tasks. It does not explicitly address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development topics, as its primary focus is on improving machine learning technology.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Hence, we propose MHR (Multi-Head Routing), which combines subsets of adapter parameters and outperforms Poly under a comparable parameter budget...

primary_category.justification: There is no direct application or discussion related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development in the paper.
primary_category.quote: We also show that MHR-µ can be used as an effective zero-shot transfer method by training the average of the pre-trained adapters for a few additional steps on the multi-task training set...

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not incorporate any secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote: This paper addresses the optimization of fine-tuning strategies in machine learning.

primary_sub_category.justification: The research focus is on machine learning advancements rather than applications in climate or sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our experimental evaluation aims to answer three research questions: 1) Does the expressivity of the routing function matter? 2) Why do routing-based PEFT methods yield superior performance? 3) Is routing useful during both multi-task pre-training and few-shot adaptation?

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no subcategories that apply to the sustainable development themes given the paper's focus on machine learning techniques.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We report the mean of the best validation accuracy for each test task. Subscripts correspond to standard deviation.

applications.justification: The technique developed is geared towards improving machine learning methods themselves and does not present application cases for sustainable development.
applications.quote: It becomes possible to fine-tune only the parameters of the routing function... resulting in highly parameter-efficient adaptation.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce or suggest a new Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category as it is not the focus of the study.
new_primary_category.quote: This establishes MHR-µ as an effective method for single-adapter fine-tuning.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no establishment of a new sub-category related to sustainable development; the focus remains technical within AI development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: During multi-task pre-training and few-shot adaptation, Poly learns both the inventory of adapters and a (continuously relaxed) binary task–module routing matrix...
